extraction.comparison_type: lowest quartile vs highest quartile of serum vitamin A
extraction.population: Men 50 years of age or older followed for a median of 10 years

sample_size.excerpt: The analytic cohort consisted of 2440 men 50 years of age or older who were followed for a median of 10 years. A total of 84 men developed prostate cancer.

cases.excerpt: A total of 84 men developed prostate cancer.

effect_size.excerpt: Considered as a continuous variable or in quartiles, a statistically significant (P less than 0.005 or P less than 0.02, respectively) trend was observed for increased risk of prostate cancer with decreasing levels of serum vitamin A. Adjusted for age and race, men in the lowest quartile had a relative risk of 2.2 (95% confidence intervals, 1.1, 4.3) compared to those in the highest quartile.
